sentences.text:
The present application under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. seeks the following prayers:-
"It is therefore most respectfully prayed that this Hoh'ble Court may kindly be pleased to allow the present application for amendment of the quashing petition in view of the aforesaid submission and in the interest of justice."
2. Issue notice.
3. Learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
Respondent no.2 appears in person and fairly does not oppose the application.
4. Accordingly, the amended petition alongwith fresh Compromise Deed dated 05.10.2023 and an affidavit of respondent no.2 are taken on record.
5. In view of the aforesaid, the application stands disposed of.

The present petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of FIR No. 700/2016, under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at PS Vasant Kunj South, Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet filed and pending before the Court of Ms. Komal Garg, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi.
7.

entities.text: Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The marriage between the petitioner no.1/husband and the respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 30.06.2013 as per Muslim Rites and Ceremony and one female child namely was born out of the said wedlock.
8. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties had been residing separately from 05.06.2016.

Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged a complaint against petitioner no. 1 (husband), petitioner no. 2 (father-in- law), petitioner no. 3 (brother-in-law), petitioner no.4 (mother-in-law) and petitioner no.5 (sister-in-law).
9.

On 05.10.2023, parties arrived at a settlement and as per the said settlement deed, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan, permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.
Therefore, the parties have agreed to abide by their reciprocal obligation as envisaged in the Settlement Deed.

10. The terms of the said Settlement Deed are extracted as under:-
"1.

That the first party has already made the payment of Rs. 5 lacs as full and final settlement for the past, present and future maintenance of the second party including all her Istridhan and dowry articles which This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/11/2023 at 21:18:27 has already been returned by the first party to the second party.
The second party shall not have any claim against the first party and neither the first party shall have any responsibility towards the second party.
Both the parties have got divorce from each other on 5.10.2023 as per Muslim Custom/Law and both the parties are at liberty to live their life as per their own wish and desire.
2. That the second party shall make the statement before the Ld. Judge at Sardhana Distt. Meerut D.P. for withdraw the FIR No. 340/2016 u/s 147/148/323/504/506/34 IPC P.S. Sardhana."
11. As per the said settlement, custody of the minor child will be with the respondent no. 2 and the petitioner no. 1 will have no visitation rights.
12. Petitioners and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, SI Lal Chand, P.S. V.K. South.

14. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

15. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303, Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
